info.desc: The Payback is the 37th studio album by American musician James Brown. The album was released in December 1973, by Polydor Records. It was originally scheduled to become the soundtrack for the blaxploitation film Hell Up in Harlem, but was rejected by the film's producers, who dismissed it as "the same old James Brown stuff." A widely repeated story—including by Brown himself—that director Larry Cohen rejected the music as "not funky enough" is denied by Cohen. podcast.body: This 37th studio album's title track, released in 1973, was James Brown's powerful opening song at Zaire 74. It is described as "the embodiment of early 70s soul" and a pinnacle of his career. "The payback is the title track to his 37th studio album of the same name."
